newsitem.title: FRANCE: Balladur wants flexible view of EMU criteria.
newsitem.headline: Balladur wants flexible view of EMU criteria.

text.p: Former French prime minister Edouard Balladur called for a flexible interpretation of the criteria for a single European currency and said major countries such as Italy and Spain should join from the start if possible.

In a France 3 television interview on Sunday night, Balladur said the Maastricht Treaty allowed the key deficit limit of three percent of gross domestic product to be judged as a trend rather than an absolute figure.

"I want these criteria to be interpreted with a bit of flexibility," said Balladur, who was conservative prime minister from 1993 to 1995 and is campaigning for the centre-right coalition in the race for May 25-June 1 parliamentary elections.

Asked whether France should make it a condition that the main Mediterranean European Union members join the euro from the start, as the Socialist opposition has advocated, Balladur said he wanted to see "the largest possible number" of countries in European economic and monetary union from the outset.
"But not at any price," he added.
Balladur said he did not believe the launch of the euro in 1999 would cause a crisis between countries which were in and those which were out.
"These difficulties will only be transitional and those countries (which are not yet in) will be in a hurry to get in as quickly as possible," he added.
On other economic issues, Balladur suggested that France should extend the maximum 18-month duration of short-term work contracts to allow greater flexibility in employment.

He stressed the need to cut taxes and reduce public spending to allow more job creation in the private sector and opposed any general reduction in working hours, noting that those countries with the lowest unemployment rate had longer working hours than France.
